mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year acceleration in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) above 3% signals stronger household demand, which typically boosts corporate earnings and equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of quarters where GDPC1 YoY growth exceeds 3%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which historically precede negative equity returns as investors anticipate weaker earnings and higher risk aversion over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE exceeds 6% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 6-month decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below 98 signals contraction in manufacturing activity, which typically precedes negative equity returns as investors anticipate lower earnings and higher recession risk over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where INDPRO remains below 98 for six months.

mechanism_narrative: A 25 basis point or greater increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals a tightening monetary cycle, which raises discount rates and typically produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by ≥ 25 bps in one month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS rises by ≥ 25 bps in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A 2% month-over-month decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) signals a sharp demand contraction, which typically precedes negative equity returns as investors anticipate weaker earnings and higher recession risk over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where GDPC1 falls by ≥ 2% month-over-month.
